text:
Sam: Heads up — customer reported resumed SSE session got routed to a different serving shard on resume. Result: doubled token billing, KV cache miss, and model variant mismatch.
Anita: Which customer? can you paste the repro and the relevant headers/logs?
Sam: Private repro uploaded (redacted): https://redwood.s3/…
Minimal client to repro:
```
curl -v \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>' \n  -H 'X-Resume-Id: abc123' \n  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \n  'https://api.redwood.dev/v1/stream?model=open-llm'
```
Server-side we see:
```
INFO route_lookup resume_id=abc123 -> shard_lookup_miss
INFO new_conn routed_to shard-9 (v1-quant)
INFO resume_conn routed_to shard-2 (v2-fp16)
```
Anita: I also see an auth rotation at 4965002475 in the logs — are resume tokens tied to the old auth key?
Max: Router currently prefers auth-token-based affinity. If auth rotated the new connection hashes differently. We should prefer resume_id affinity when present.
Priya: Console currently attributes token usage to the new connection id, so billing duplicates. Proposal: use resume_id as the primary key for billing aggregation when present, and add a "resume_count" metric.
Sam: :thumbsup: Also observed semantic drift — resumed session landed on a different model variant (v1 vs v2) so outputs differ.
Anita: If we change routing to prefer resume_id, we must ensure sticky shard mappings are durable across restarts and multi-region route tables.
Max: Another wrinkle: sometimes mapping is GC'd quickly. If mapping missing we either fallback to best-effort routing (current) or return an error. I think we need a header-level opt-in.
Priya: Telemetry request: add `resume_affinity_key` to route logs and surface a new console panel showing resume-mismatch rate by tenant. Sampling 100% for first 48h of rollout, then 1%.
Sam: Quick patch idea: Router rule: if `X-Resume-Id` present -> lookup sticky mapping and force route. If mapping missing and client sends `X-Resume-Mode: strict` -> return 409 with `Retry-Without-Resume` hint. Default to `best-effort` to avoid breakage.
Anita: Returning 409 might break clients that expect transparent resume. We should spec SDK behavior before shipping any strict mode default. Also add UX in rollout console to flag resume mismatches during canary.
Max: Suggest exposing `X-Resume-Mode: strict|best-effort` in SDKs. Default stays `best-effort`. Admins can opt in to strict in Dedicated/private setups.
Priya: I'll open telemetry PR to add resume_id tags, a billing dedupe rule (dedupe by resume_id within a 5m window), and a console widget for resume anomalies.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary/routable-resume-fix -> build #7852 (ETA ~15m)
Sam: Filed issue #4302 and a short RFC draft: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/4302 — assigning Anita + Priya to own. Will dogfood in canary tomorrow and follow up with a postmortem if we see customer impact.
